texts: Three-dimensional TEE is the most appropriate test before percutaneous closure of an ASD: B.
It shows the size and shape of the defect and the length of every rim, which decide whether a device can be anchored and which size to choose.
TEE also guides the device during closure and checks for other defects and for the drainage of the pulmonary veins.
Transthoracic echo is often enough in small children but sees the rims less well in adults; MRI, CT and catheterization add less for this purpose.
In the picture, the bat inside the sofa slide wears 3D glasses and sees the hole and its rims in depth, while the cufflinks wait.
Memory hook: the bat in 3D glasses measures the rims before the cufflinks go in.
